blocks.passage:
Business is international. Every day, we work with people from different countries.

Different cultures have different habits. Some people speak directly, others more softly. Some start meetings on time, others chat first. None of them are wrong — they are just different.

The best tool is curiosity. Ask questions with respect. "How do you usually start meetings in your country?" is a great way to learn and build a friendly relationship.

audio.text:
I'm about to work with a new team in Japan, and before the first meeting, I'm doing something simple but powerful: I'm asking questions to understand their style. I don't assume mine is the right one.

Back home, I'm quite direct — I say what I think quickly. But I've read that in Japan, people are often more soft-spoken, and there's more silence, and that silence is normal and comfortable. So I won't rush to fill it.

I also learned that they may not say 'no' directly. A soft 'that might be difficult' can mean no. So I'll listen carefully, not just to the words.

And I'll ask, with respect: 'How do you usually like to run meetings? I want to work in a way that's comfortable for you.' People love that question. It shows curiosity, not judgement.

None of this means I change who I am. It just means I'm curious and respectful. Different isn't wrong — it's just different. Ask, listen, adapt a little, and the relationship starts warm.
